title: A new planning question
body: Imagine a community garden choosing between a larger growing area and a smaller one with vegetation and a storage feature. No drainage survey is available. What should the group check before choosing?

choices.text: Choose the largest growing area; meeting demand settles the decision.
choices.explanation: Growing space matters, but this skips vegetation, costs and water. Compare those needs before deciding which design fits.

choices.text: Choose the storage feature; it will handle runoff from every plot.
choices.explanation: Storage is finite. In this game it only retains runoff from its connected area. Without drainage information, its benefit to each plot is uncertain.

choices.text: Compare growing needs, cover, costs, drainage connections and storage capacity under the same storm.
choices.explanation: Yes. Compare the competing needs and find the missing drainage information. Neither larger growing space nor more storage is automatically best for every place.

choices.text: Replace all growing space with vegetation; productive needs can wait.
choices.explanation: Vegetation can be part of a plan, but this discards the stated growing need. Look for a workable balance and check the assumptions behind the water estimate.
